hypothesis: The backend's standard Welford LayerNorm can reduce accumulated normalization discrepancy while retaining a standard operator boundary for future autodiff. Numerical closeness to the Python CPU implementation is a hypothesis, not guaranteed by Welford stability.
candidate: burn::tensor::module::layer_norm(x, gamma, Some(beta), 1e-5), unchanged Flex CPU/std features; apply uniformly to all seven model LayerNorm modules if the local gate passes

source_basis.distinction: PyTorch uses vectorized Welford and cascade merging; scalar Flex uses serial Welford and folds inv_std*gamma before centered multiplication. These are different operation orders; no bit-exact equivalence or backward correctness is assumed.

local_gate.baseline_replay: all 49 baseline outputs byte-exact against saved RP outputs
local_gate.aggregate_squared_error: strictly lower than baseline across all 49 same-input comparisons
local_gate.case_squared_error: no increase in any of the seven cases, summing all seven modules
local_gate.decision_inputs: all elements only; no use of the known failing point or selected module

confirmation: Only if the local gate passes: one uniform model change, existing three Rust tests, one fixed seven-case forward and original R1 comparison over all 23 anchors. Adopt only if the entire original gate passes; otherwise restore the original core bytes and retain the rejected candidate source and outputs. No second candidate or retry after a scientific failure.
stop: One candidate, 49 same-input calls and 49 baseline reproductions. A failed local gate ends this experiment without full forward or core changes. No reference regeneration, target/truth access, training, tolerance change, dependency change, or R2 start.
